basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A position is a post that exists independently of whoever holds it; occupancy is a separate assignment (WM-ORG-016).
It is distinct from a job class or occupation, which classify many positions.
It differs from a job advertisement, which announces an opening for a position.
One position can have several occupants at once or none, governed by its type and headcount.

may: Draft a position description from approved requirements and functions.
Compute vacancy from occupancy records and report it with time.
Map a position to an occupation classifier with its version.
Publish an approved position projection to a job board.
mustNot: Store occupant names or personal data on the position record.
Advertise or fill a position before classification, requirements and screening designation are approved.
Read or disclose pay ranges or risk designations outside the allowed roles.
Persist vacancy as an independent fact that can diverge from occupancy.
requiresHuman: Classifying, grading or reclassifying a position.
Authorizing a fill, freeze or abolition.
Deciding an appeal against a position description or grade.

considerations: Position requirements must not exclude people on protected grounds unless the requirement is genuinely essential.
Pay transparency and fair grading affect equal pay between groups.
Abolishing positions affects livelihoods; decisions should be recorded and contestable.

items: A position has an identifier, a title, a unit, a grade or class and a headcount, with or without an occupant.
Confused with a person's job, an employment contract, a role in an access system and a job posting.
Discriminatory requirements built into a position description.
Access or authority granted to a position persists after the occupant leaves.
Disclosure of pay or security designation data to unauthorized readers.
ISCO-08 International Standard Classification of Occupations.
ESCO European Skills, Competences, Qualifications and Occupations.
HR Open Standards for position and recruiting data exchange.
